subject: Clarify: private deployment pen-test evidence, jurisdiction & egress matrix
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@finedge.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: secops@finedge.com
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Pen test evidence for FinEdge private deployment — jurisdiction & egress details

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the architecture review last week. As part of our SIG and CAIQ workstream, we need a couple of concrete artefacts tied to the private deployment (FinEdge production VPC in eu-west-1) before our auditors sign off: 

- A short explanation of the tested boundary assumptions for the customer-hosted instance (what was in-scope vs out-of-scope). We specifically need to know how Redwood defines the tenant boundary in a private VPC deployment when using Transit Gateway and managed NATs.
- An "egress matrix" that lists all outbound destinations observed during the pen test (IP ranges, FQDNs, purpose) and which hosts/processes initiated them. This is mandatory for our data residency and third-party access logs.
- Proof of segmentation controls (security groups, NACLs, and any overlay policies) that were validated during the test. Screenshots or sanitized config snippets are fine.

We have a slightly accelerated audit window (auditors requested submission by Mar 8). Can your team provide an evidence bundle (PDF summary + attachments) and a short commentary about how egress is handled for customers who use private KMS/HSM in their cloud account?

If easier, we can take a 30-min call to walk the auditors through it.

Appreciate your help — Olivia

--
Olivia Park
Security Assurance Lead
FinEdge Bank
---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@finedge.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pen test evidence for FinEdge private deployment — jurisdiction & egress details

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list. I'm putting together a short package and will attach the high-level pen test executive summary and the raw egress matrix export. Quick notes so you know what to expect: 

- Boundary assumptions: the pen test targeted the Redwood runtime inside the customer VPC (private subnets hosting inference workers) plus the edge proxy layer (customer-managed private endpoints). Control-plane services (our control plane in a Redwood account) were out of scope except for the authentication handshake points. The attached summary spells this out and includes the exact subnets and instance tags used in the test.

- Egress matrix: we captured outbound flows from the worker instances during test scenarios (uploads to S3 in your account, telemetry to our metrics endpoint (only over mTLS when enabled), TLS handshakes to certificate authorities for OCSP). The matrix will include destination CIDRs and observed FQDNs. We redacted private IPs/hostnames.

- Segmentation evidence: I'll include sanitized security group rules and a short packet-capture excerpt showing denied traffic to an emulated external host (proof of NACL enforcement).

Question for FinEdge: do you want the egress matrix to be split by region (eu-west-1) or by process (runtime, sidecars, control-plane callbacks)? We can produce both but want to prioritize the format your auditors prefer.

Attaching: redwood-private-pt-executive-summary.pdf; customer-vpc-egress-matrix.xlsx (redacted).

If you'd like a call, I can loop Vivek and Karthik for technical detail.

Thanks,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Product Security Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-private-pt-executive-summary.pdf (summary), customer-vpc-egress-matrix.xlsx (redacted)

From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@finedge.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, secops@finedge.com
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 08:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pen test evidence for FinEdge private deployment — jurisdiction & egress details

Marissa — this looks good, thank you. Two follow-ups from SecOps: 

1) Jurisdiction/Residency: can you confirm whether any telemetry or debug logs were written to Redwood-managed storage during test runs? FinEdge policy requires logs containing any FinEdge PII or cardholder tokens to remain in our account. We need a signed assertion that no PII left the customer account during tests.

2) KMS/HSM: our architects need a short note about key usage. In our configuration we used customer-managed KMS keys for model encryption at rest. Did the pen test exercise any paths that required Redwood-managed KMS access or HSM calls? If so, please enumerate.

If you can add one paragraph to the executive summary answering the two bullets above we can keep the auditors happy. If not, SecOps wants an attestation email from Redwood security.

Thanks — Olivia

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@finedge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 05 Mar 2027 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pen test evidence for FinEdge private deployment — jurisdiction & egress details

Hi Olivia,

Appreciate the patience — quick answers below and next steps. We'll produce a 1-page attestation as requested and update the executive summary with the two clarifications.

- Telemetry/log residency: During the test runs we used agent-side local logging that writes to S3 buckets in your FinEdge account (the test harness assumes the customer's storage). No FinEdge PII or tokens were exfiltrated to Redwood-managed storage. We verified object writes to your S3 and then ran teardown scripts that left only audit logs. We will provide the audit-log summary (bucket, object prefixes, and timestamps) in the evidence bundle.

- KMS/HSM usage: For this engagement the model artifacts and disk volumes were encrypted with your customer-managed KMS keys. Redwood did not use Redwood-managed KMS or HSM calls that would cause key material to leave FinEdge control. The test did exercise runtime calls that used the KMS Decrypt API in your account (via IAM role assumed by the worker nodes) — we will enumerate the exact API calls and timestamps in the attestation.

Next steps: Marissa and Karthik will assemble a short attestation (signed by Product Security), a sanitized egress matrix split by process, and the small packet-capture snippets for segmentation proof. Expect the bundle by EOD Mar 6 so you can share with auditors on Mar 8. If SecOps still wants a 30-min walkthrough, propose Tue Mar 9 09:00-09:30 CET and we'll confirm.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Security
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments referenced in thread: redwood-private-pt-executive-summary.pdf, customer-vpc-egress-matrix.xlsx
